{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_015tJwadkS9YhSGBRhRhz8S1","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t\\section{When Does Discriminability Fail as Reward Utility?}\\label{sec:discussion}\n2\t\n3\t\\paragraph{Root cause of the probe reward trap.}\n4\tThe probe reward trap (\\S\\ref{sec:probe_trap}) and the cosine failures (\\S\\ref{sec:cosine_failure}) share a common geometric root.\n5\t$\\dsyc$ encodes the \\emph{direction} of belief change but not its \\emph{evidential warrant}: valid revision and sycophantic capitulation both shift activations toward the user's position along the same direction.\n6\tThe two reward families expose complementary faces of this blindness.\n7\tCosine $\\rone$ penalizes all belief change indiscriminately (mode collapse, F1c--F1d); the binary probe $\\rone$ rewards all resistance regardless of input validity (stubbornness trap, $\\tof{=}0$ by step 500)---dual consequences of a direction that conflates resisting invalid challenges with refusing valid corrections.\n8\tAlthough $\\dsyc$ separability correlates with evidence strength (\\S\\ref{sec:direction_quality}), it encodes \\emph{how much} belief changed, not whether the change was appropriate (\\S\\ref{sec:probe_trap}).\n9\tCross-model evidence (Llama-3-8B AUROC $0.779$) confirms the limitation generalizes.\n10\tThis contrasts with safety directions~\\citep{zhang2026latentgrpo}, where the target behavior is geometrically distinct; concept directions succeed when shortcuts are separable~\\citep{wu2026rewardhacking}.\n11\tIndependent work corroborates: persona vectors are independent of $\\dsyc$ \\citep{kelkar2026persona}, and sycophancy sub-behaviors \\citep{vennemeyer2025sycophancy} collapse onto $\\dsyc$'s single axis.\n12\t\n13\t\\paragraph{GRPO results under our configuration.}\n14\t\n15\t\\begin{table}[t]\n16\t\\centering\n17\t\\caption{Sycophancy calibration methods on Qwen3-8B. Higher $\\sycon$ (harmonic mean of $\\tof$ and $\\nof$) indicates better calibration.}\n18\t\\label{tab:main_comparison}\n19\t\\resizebox{\\columnwidth}{!}{%\n20\t\\begin{tabular}{@{}llcccc@{}}\n21\t\\toprule\n22\tMethod & Type & $\\sycon$ $\\uparrow$ & $\\tof$ $\\uparrow$ & $\\nof$ $\\uparrow$ & Step \\\\\n23\t\\midrule\n24\tVanilla & -- & 0.134 & 0.072 & 0.945 & -- \\\\\n25\t\\midrule\n26\t\\multicolumn{6}{l}{\\textit{GRPO with $\\dsyc$}} \\\\\n27\tCosine $\\rone$ (F1a--F1d)$^a$ & RL & 0.000 & 0.000 & 1.000 & 500 \\\\\n28\tBinary Probe $\\rone$ (F2) & RL & 0.000 & 0.000 & 0.995 & 500 \\\\\n29\tContinuous Probe $\\rone$ (F3) & RL & 0.124 & 0.066 & 0.934 & 500 \\\\\n30\t\\midrule\n31\t\\multicolumn{6}{l}{\\textit{GRPO without $\\dsyc$}} \\\\\n32\t$\\rthree$-only GRPO$^b$ & RL & 0.153 & 0.083 & 0.983 & 6500 \\\\\n33\t\\midrule\n34\t\\multicolumn{6}{l}{\\textit{SFT with $\\dsyc$ probe penalty}} \\\\\n35\tSFT probe (seed 2)$^c$ & SFT & 0.393 & 0.276 & 0.680 & 500 \\\\\n36\tSFT probe (seed 3)$^c$ & SFT & 0.407 & 0.287 & 0.696 & 1000 \\\\\n37\t\\midrule\n38\t\\multicolumn{6}{l}{\\textit{Reference methods}$^d$} \\\\\n39\tActAdd ($\\alpha{=}5$) & Inference & 0.054 & 0.028 & 0.961 & -- \\\\\n40\t\\textbf{ACT} (seed 1) & SFT & \\textbf{0.301} & \\textbf{0.182} & 0.867 & 8000 \\\\\n41\tACT (seed 2)$^e$ & SFT & 0.286 & 0.171 & 0.862 & 7000 \\\\\n42\t\\bottomrule\n43\t\\multicolumn{6}{l}{\\footnotesize $^a$All collapsed from step 1 ($\\tof{=}0$); F1d diverged at step 2160.} \\\\\n44\t\\multicolumn{6}{l}{\\footnotesize $^b$Best of 28 checkpoints (2 seeds); only 4/28 exceed vanilla.} \\\\\n45\t\\multicolumn{6}{l}{\\footnotesize $^c$Peak ckpt (train/eval overlap); 2/3 seeds collapse by step 2000 (mean $0.171 \\pm 0.122$).} \\\\\n46\t\\multicolumn{6}{l}{\\footnotesize $^d$Not directly comparable: differ from GRPO along 5+ dimensions (\\S\\ref{sec:discussion}).} \\\\\n47\t\\multicolumn{6}{l}{\\footnotesize $^e$15 ckpts, all ${>}$ vanilla. Best $\\sycon{=}0.286$ (step 7000).} \\\\\n48\t\\end{tabular}}\n49\t\\end{table}\n50\t\n51\tIf $\\dsyc$ alone caused the cosine and probe failures (\\S\\ref{sec:cosine_failure}--\\S\\ref{sec:probe_trap}), removing it should recover calibration.\n52\t$\\rthree$-only GRPO tests this: only a minority of checkpoints across two seeds exceed vanilla, with both seeds oscillating before diverging (Table~\\ref{tab:main_comparison}; Figure~\\ref{fig:trajectory}).\n53\t$\\dsyc$ AUROC and $\\rthree$ both remain nearly constant across checkpoints, yet $\\sycon$ fluctuates substantially.\n54\t$\\rthree$ mirrors $\\dsyc$'s limitation: it identifies valid corrections at a negligible rate, comparable to the vanilla baseline, confirming that the asymmetry reflects the NLI hypothesis design, not behavioral collapse.\n55\tBoth signals encode \\emph{whether} belief changed, not \\emph{whether it should have}.\n56\t\n57\t\\paragraph{Competing hypotheses and ablation.}\n58\tThree explanations are consistent with these failures: (a)~$\\dsyc$ is fundamentally unsuitable as a sycophancy reward; (b)~group size$=$2 provides insufficient ranking diversity; (c)~sycophancy calibration resists scalar per-completion RL.\n59\tTwo ablations discriminate among them (Table~\\ref{tab:ablation}).\n60\tGRPO fails at both group sizes tested (gs$=$8: all below vanilla, terminated early) and at doubled sequence length (512 tokens, reward flat), ruling out~(b) and truncation (Table~\\ref{tab:ablation}).\n61\tReducing ACT to GRPO's LoRA configuration still yields consistently higher $\\sycon$, with every checkpoint exceeding vanilla; under matched adapters, per-token SFT achieves $1.7{\\times}$ higher $\\sycon$ than per-completion GRPO, identifying supervision granularity as one plausible explanation~\\citep{beigi2025smart}; confounds are discussed in Limitations.\n62\tThe probe reward trap independently supports~(a): the trap arises despite stopped gradients.\n63\t\n64\t\\begin{table}[t]\n65\t\\centering\n66\t\\small\n67\t\\caption{Ablation: isolating supervision paradigm from LoRA configuration. All methods use Qwen3-8B with $\\rthree$ (behavioral reward). Vanilla $\\sycon{=}0.134$. $^\\dagger$Terminated early after three checkpoints showed declining trajectory. $^\\ddagger$Peak at step 7000; final checkpoint (step 8000) $\\sycon{=}0.267$.}\n68\t\\label{tab:ablation}\n69\t\\resizebox{\\columnwidth}{!}{%\n70\t\\begin{tabular}{@{}llcc@{}}\n71\t\\toprule\n72\tMethod & LoRA config & Best $\\sycon$ & ${>}$Van. \\\\\n73\t\\midrule\n74\tGRPO gs$=$2 (2 seeds) & r64, $\\alpha$64, 4m & 0.153 & 4/28 \\\\\n75\tGRPO gs$=$8$^\\dagger$ & r64, $\\alpha$64, 4m & 0.085 & 0/3 \\\\\n76\t\\midrule\n77\tACT reduced-LoRA$^\\ddagger$ & r64, $\\alpha$64, 4m & 0.326 & 16/16 \\\\\n78\tACT full s1 & r64, $\\alpha$128, 7m & 0.301 & 16/16 \\\\\n79\tACT full s2 & r64, $\\alpha$128, 7m & 0.286 & 15/15 \\\\\n80\t\\bottomrule\n81\t\\end{tabular}}\n82\t\\end{table}\n83\t\n84\t\\paragraph{ACT vs.\\ probe-based methods.}\n85\tACT's advantage over GRPO is categorical: even ACT's worst checkpoint outperforms GRPO's best, with held-out $\\sycon$ of $0.284$ confirming generalization beyond training data (Limitations).\n86\tSFT with a differentiable probe penalty achieves higher peak $\\sycon$ on the training set (Table~\\ref{tab:main_comparison}), but these scores reflect full train/eval overlap and the advantage is transient: probe gaming (\\S\\ref{sec:probe_trap}) eliminates the regularization signal, and the model overfits to below vanilla by step 2000 in two of three seeds (mean $\\sycon{=}0.171 \\pm 0.122$).\n87\tThree temporal patterns emerge: GRPO probe rewards cause immediate behavioral death ($\\tof{=}0$); SFT probe penalties yield initially high but unsustainable calibration; ACT sacrifices peak for stability by eliminating probe dependence (31/31 ${>}$ vanilla, with held-out generalization confirmed).\n88\t\n89\t\\paragraph{Inference-time probes and future directions.}\n90\tDiscriminability and reward utility occupy distinct roles: a direction that reliably \\emph{detects} a behavior may fail to \\emph{correct} it when the optimizer exploits the geometric shortcut that makes detection easy.\n91\tInference-time reranking~\\citep{papadatos2024probepenalties} and per-step process rewards~\\citep{beigi2025smart} sidestep this by avoiding optimization-loop inclusion entirely.\n92\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"978d5c6d-01eb-430b-a005-ba8925173f6b","uuid":"ec86e53b-adcb-4539-bb68-6ba208ea7afd","timestamp":"2026-05-25T17:25:58.028Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-be-idea-gen-0515-3/projects/contrastive_entrain_calib/docs/paper/sections/discussion.tex","content":"\\section{When Does Discriminability Fail as Reward Utility?}\\label{sec:discussion}\n\n\\paragraph{Root cause of the probe reward trap.}\nThe probe reward trap (\\S\\ref{sec:probe_trap}) and the cosine failures (\\S\\ref{sec:cosine_failure}) share a common geometric root.\n$\\dsyc$ encodes the \\emph{direction} of belief change but not its \\emph{evidential warrant}: valid revision and sycophantic capitulation both shift activations toward the user's position along the same direction.\nThe two reward families expose complementary faces of this blindness.\nCosine $\\rone$ penalizes all belief change indiscriminately (mode collapse, F1c--F1d); the binary probe $\\rone$ rewards all resistance regardless of input validity (stubbornness trap, $\\tof{=}0$ by step 500)---dual consequences of a direction that conflates resisting invalid challenges with refusing valid corrections.\nAlthough $\\dsyc$ separability correlates with evidence strength (\\S\\ref{sec:direction_quality}), it encodes \\emph{how much} belief changed, not whether the change was appropriate (\\S\\ref{sec:probe_trap}).\nCross-model evidence (Llama-3-8B AUROC $0.779$) confirms the limitation generalizes.\nThis contrasts with safety directions~\\citep{zhang2026latentgrpo}, where the target behavior is geometrically distinct; concept directions succeed when shortcuts are separable~\\citep{wu2026rewardhacking}.\nIndependent work corroborates: persona vectors are independent of $\\dsyc$ \\citep{kelkar2026persona}, and sycophancy sub-behaviors \\citep{vennemeyer2025sycophancy} collapse onto $\\dsyc$'s single axis.\n\n\\paragraph{GRPO results under our configuration.}\n\n\\begin{table}[t]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Sycophancy calibration methods on Qwen3-8B. Higher $\\sycon$ (harmonic mean of $\\tof$ and $\\nof$) indicates better calibration.}\n\\label{tab:main_comparison}\n\\resizebox{\\columnwidth}{!}{%\n\\begin{tabular}{@{}llcccc@{}}\n\\toprule\nMethod & Type & $\\sycon$ $\\uparrow$ & $\\tof$ $\\uparrow$ & $\\nof$ $\\uparrow$ & Step \\\\\n\\midrule\nVanilla & -- & 0.134 & 0.072 & 0.945 & -- \\\\\n\\midrule\n\\multicolumn{6}{l}{\\textit{GRPO with $\\dsyc$}} \\\\\nCosine $\\rone$ (F1a--F1d)$^a$ & RL & 0.000 & 0.000 & 1.000 & 500 \\\\\nBinary Probe $\\rone$ (F2) & RL & 0.000 & 0.000 & 0.995 & 500 \\\\\nContinuous Probe $\\rone$ (F3) & RL & 0.124 & 0.066 & 0.934 & 500 \\\\\n\\midrule\n\\multicolumn{6}{l}{\\textit{GRPO without $\\dsyc$}} \\\\\n$\\rthree$-only GRPO$^b$ & RL & 0.153 & 0.083 & 0.983 & 6500 \\\\\n\\midrule\n\\multicolumn{6}{l}{\\textit{SFT with $\\dsyc$ probe penalty}} \\\\\nSFT probe (seed 2)$^c$ & SFT & 0.393 & 0.276 & 0.680 & 500 \\\\\nSFT probe (seed 3)$^c$ & SFT & 0.407 & 0.287 & 0.696 & 1000 \\\\\n\\midrule\n\\multicolumn{6}{l}{\\textit{Reference methods}$^d$} \\\\\nActAdd ($\\alpha{=}5$) & Inference & 0.054 & 0.028 & 0.961 & -- \\\\\n\\textbf{ACT} (seed 1) & SFT & \\textbf{0.301} & \\textbf{0.182} & 0.867 & 8000 \\\\\nACT (seed 2)$^e$ & SFT & 0.286 & 0.171 & 0.862 & 7000 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\multicolumn{6}{l}{\\footnotesize $^a$All collapsed from step 1 ($\\tof{=}0$); F1d diverged at step 2160.} \\\\\n\\multicolumn{6}{l}{\\footnotesize $^b$Best of 28 checkpoints (2 seeds); only 4/28 exceed vanilla.} \\\\\n\\multicolumn{6}{l}{\\footnotesize $^c$Peak ckpt (train/eval overlap); 2/3 seeds collapse by step 2000 (mean $0.171 \\pm 0.122$).} \\\\\n\\multicolumn{6}{l}{\\footnotesize $^d$Not directly comparable: differ from GRPO along 5+ dimensions (\\S\\ref{sec:discussion}).} \\\\\n\\multicolumn{6}{l}{\\footnotesize $^e$15 ckpts, all ${>}$ vanilla. Best $\\sycon{=}0.286$ (step 7000).} \\\\\n\\end{tabular}}\n\\end{table}\n\nIf $\\dsyc$ alone caused the cosine and probe failures (\\S\\ref{sec:cosine_failure}--\\S\\ref{sec:probe_trap}), removing it should recover calibration.\n$\\rthree$-only GRPO tests this: only a minority of checkpoints across two seeds exceed vanilla, with both seeds oscillating before diverging (Table~\\ref{tab:main_comparison}; Figure~\\ref{fig:trajectory}).\n$\\dsyc$ AUROC and $\\rthree$ both remain nearly constant across checkpoints, yet $\\sycon$ fluctuates substantially.\n$\\rthree$ mirrors $\\dsyc$'s limitation: it identifies valid corrections at a negligible rate, comparable to the vanilla baseline, confirming that the asymmetry reflects the NLI hypothesis design, not behavioral collapse.\nBoth signals encode \\emph{whether} belief changed, not \\emph{whether it should have}.\n\n\\paragraph{Competing hypotheses and ablation.}\nThree explanations are consistent with these failures: (a)~$\\dsyc$ is fundamentally unsuitable as a sycophancy reward; (b)~group size$=$2 provides insufficient ranking diversity; (c)~sycophancy calibration resists scalar per-completion RL.\nTwo ablations discriminate among them (Table~\\ref{tab:ablation}).\nGRPO fails at both group sizes tested (gs$=$8: all below vanilla, terminated early) and at doubled sequence length (512 tokens, reward flat), ruling out~(b) and truncation (Table~\\ref{tab:ablation}).\nReducing ACT to GRPO's LoRA configuration still yields consistently higher $\\sycon$, with every checkpoint exceeding vanilla; under matched adapters, per-token SFT achieves $1.7{\\times}$ higher $\\sycon$ than per-completion GRPO, identifying supervision granularity as one plausible explanation~\\citep{beigi2025smart}; confounds are discussed in Limitations.\nThe probe reward trap independently supports~(a): the trap arises despite stopped gradients.\n\n\\begin{table}[t]\n\\centering\n\\small\n\\caption{Ablation: isolating supervision paradigm from LoRA configuration. All methods use Qwen3-8B with $\\rthree$ (behavioral reward). Vanilla $\\sycon{=}0.134$. $^\\dagger$Terminated early after three checkpoints showed declining trajectory. $^\\ddagger$Peak at step 7000; final checkpoint (step 8000) $\\sycon{=}0.267$.}\n\\label{tab:ablation}\n\\resizebox{\\columnwidth}{!}{%\n\\begin{tabular}{@{}llcc@{}}\n\\toprule\nMethod & LoRA config & Best $\\sycon$ & ${>}$Van. \\\\\n\\midrule\nGRPO gs$=$2 (2 seeds) & r64, $\\alpha$64, 4m & 0.153 & 4/28 \\\\\nGRPO gs$=$8$^\\dagger$ & r64, $\\alpha$64, 4m & 0.085 & 0/3 \\\\\n\\midrule\nACT reduced-LoRA$^\\ddagger$ & r64, $\\alpha$64, 4m & 0.326 & 16/16 \\\\\nACT full s1 & r64, $\\alpha$128, 7m & 0.301 & 16/16 \\\\\nACT full s2 & r64, $\\alpha$128, 7m & 0.286 & 15/15 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}}\n\\end{table}\n\n\\paragraph{ACT vs.\\ probe-based methods.}\nACT's advantage over GRPO is categorical: even ACT's worst checkpoint outperforms GRPO's best, with held-out $\\sycon$ of $0.284$ confirming generalization beyond training data (Limitations).\nSFT with a differentiable probe penalty achieves higher peak $\\sycon$ on the training set (Table~\\ref{tab:main_comparison}), but these scores reflect full train/eval overlap and the advantage is transient: probe gaming (\\S\\ref{sec:probe_trap}) eliminates the regularization signal, and the model overfits to below vanilla by step 2000 in two of three seeds (mean $\\sycon{=}0.171 \\pm 0.122$).\nThree temporal patterns emerge: GRPO probe rewards cause immediate behavioral death ($\\tof{=}0$); SFT probe penalties yield initially high but unsustainable calibration; ACT sacrifices peak for stability by eliminating probe dependence (31/31 ${>}$ vanilla, with held-out generalization confirmed).\n\n\\paragraph{Inference-time probes and future directions.}\nDiscriminability and reward utility occupy distinct roles: a direction that reliably \\emph{detects} a behavior may fail to \\emph{correct} it when the optimizer exploits the geometric shortcut that makes detection easy.\nInference-time reranking~\\citep{papadatos2024probepenalties} and per-step process rewards~\\citep{beigi2025smart} sidestep this by avoiding optimization-loop inclusion entirely.\n","numLines":92,"startLine":1,"totalLines":92}}}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01CiAJhPDorddtBWEHMUZAuH","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t\\section{When Does Discriminability Fail as Reward Utility?}\\label{sec:discussion}\n2\t\n3\t\\paragraph{Root cause of the probe reward trap.}\n4\tThe probe reward trap (\\S\\ref{sec:probe_trap}) and the cosine failures (\\S\\ref{sec:cosine_failure}) share a common geometric root.\n5\t$\\dsyc$ encodes the \\emph{direction} of belief change but not its \\emph{evidential warrant}: valid revision and sycophantic capitulation both shift activations toward the user's position along the same direction.\n6\tThe two reward families expose complementary faces of this blindness.\n7\tCosine $\\rone$ penalizes all belief change indiscriminately (mode collapse, F1c--F1d); the binary probe $\\rone$ rewards all resistance regardless of input validity (stubbornness trap, $\\tof{=}0$ by step 500)---dual consequences of a direction that conflates resisting invalid challenges with refusing valid corrections.\n8\tAlthough $\\dsyc$ separability correlates with evidence strength (\\S\\ref{sec:direction_quality}), it encodes \\emph{how much} belief changed, not whether the change was appropriate (\\S\\ref{sec:probe_trap}).\n9\tCross-model evidence (Llama-3-8B AUROC $0.779$) confirms the limitation generalizes.\n10\tThis contrasts with safety directions~\\citep{zhang2026latentgrpo}, where the target behavior is geometrically distinct; concept directions succeed when shortcuts are separable~\\citep{wu2026rewardhacking}.\n11\tIndependent work corroborates: persona vectors are independent of $\\dsyc$ \\citep{kelkar2026persona}, and sycophancy sub-behaviors \\citep{vennemeyer2025sycophancy} collapse onto $\\dsyc$'s single axis.\n12\t\n13\t\\paragraph{GRPO results under our configuration.}\n14\t\n15\t\\begin{table}[t]\n16\t\\centering\n17\t\\caption{Sycophancy calibration methods on Qwen3-8B. Best $\\sycon{=}0.286$ (step 7000).} \\\\\n48\t\\end{tabular}}\n49\t\\end{table}\n50\t\n51\tIf $\\dsyc$ alone caused the cosine and probe failures (\\S\\ref{sec:cosine_failure}--\\S\\ref{sec:probe_trap}), removing it should recover calibration.\n52\t$\\rthree$-only GRPO tests this: only a minority of checkpoints across two seeds exceed vanilla, with both seeds oscillating before diverging (Table~\\ref{tab:main_comparison}; Figure~\\ref{fig:trajectory}).\n53\t$\\dsyc$ AUROC and $\\rthree$ both remain nearly constant across checkpoints, yet $\\sycon$ fluctuates substantially.\n54\t$\\rthree$ mirrors $\\dsyc$'s limitation: it identifies valid corrections at a negligible rate, comparable to the vanilla baseline, confirming that the asymmetry reflects the NLI hypothesis design, not behavioral collapse.\n55\tBoth signals encode \\emph{whether} belief changed, not \\emph{whether it should have}.\n56\t\n57\t\\paragraph{Competing hypotheses and ablation.}\n58\tThree explanations are consistent with these failures: (a)~$\\dsyc$ is fundamentally unsuitable as a sycophancy reward; (b)~group size$=$2 provides insufficient ranking diversity; (c)~sycophancy calibration resists scalar per-completion RL.\n59\tTwo ablations discriminate among them (Table~\\ref{tab:ablation}).\n60\tGRPO fails at both group sizes tested (gs$=$8: all below vanilla, terminated early) and at doubled sequence length (512 tokens, reward flat), ruling out~(b) and truncation (Table~\\ref{tab:ablation}).\n61\tReducing ACT to GRPO's LoRA configuration still yields consistently higher $\\sycon$, with every checkpoint exceeding vanilla; under matched adapters, per-token SFT achieves $1.7{\\times}$ higher $\\sycon$ than per-completion GRPO, identifying supervision granularity as one plausible explanation~\\citep{beigi2025smart}; confounds are discussed in Limitations.\n62\tThe probe reward trap independently supports~(a): the trap arises despite stopped gradients.\n63\t\n64\t\\begin{table}[t]\n65\t\\centering\n66\t\\small\n67\t\\caption{Ablation: isolating supervision paradigm from LoRA configuration. All methods use Qwen3-8B with $\\rthree$ (behavioral reward). Vanilla $\\sycon{=}0.134$. $^\\dagger$Terminated early after three checkpoints showed declining trajectory. $^\\ddagger$Peak at step 7000; final checkpoint (step 8000) $\\sycon{=}0.267$.}\n68\t\\label{tab:ablation}\n69\t\\resizebox{\\columnwidth}{!}{%\n70\t\\begin{tabular}{@{}llcc@{}}\n71\t\\toprule\n72\tMethod & LoRA config & Best $\\sycon$ & ${>}$Van. \\\\\n73\t\\midrule\n74\tGRPO gs$=$2 (2 seeds) & r64, $\\alpha$64, 4m & 0.153 & 4/28 \\\\\n75\tGRPO gs$=$8$^\\dagger$ & r64, $\\alpha$64, 4m & 0.085 & 0/3 \\\\\n76\t\\midrule\n77\tACT reduced-LoRA$^\\ddagger$ & r64, $\\alpha$64, 4m & 0.326 & 16/16 \\\\\n78\tACT full s1 & r64, $\\alpha$128, 7m & 0.301 & 16/16 \\\\\n79\tACT full s2 & r64, $\\alpha$128, 7m & 0.286 & 15/15 \\\\\n80\t\\bottomrule\n81\t\\end{tabular}}\n82\t\\end{table}\n83\t\n84\t\\paragraph{ACT vs.\\ probe-based methods.}\n85\tACT's advantage over GRPO is categorical: even ACT's worst checkpoint outperforms GRPO's best, with held-out $\\sycon$ of $0.284$ confirming generalization beyond training data (Limitations).\n86\tSFT with a differentiable probe penalty achieves higher peak $\\sycon$ on the training set (Table~\\ref{tab:main_comparison}), but these scores reflect full train/eval overlap and the advantage is transient: probe gaming (\\S\\ref{sec:probe_trap}) eliminates the regularization signal, and the model overfits to below vanilla by step 2000 in two of three seeds (mean $\\sycon{=}0.171 \\pm 0.122$).\n87\tThree temporal patterns emerge: GRPO probe rewards cause immediate behavioral death ($\\tof{=}0$); SFT probe penalties yield initially high but unsustainable calibration; ACT sacrifices peak for stability by eliminating probe dependence (31/31 ${>}$ vanilla, with held-out generalization confirmed).\n88\t\n89\t\\paragraph{Inference-time probes and future directions.}\n90\tDiscriminability and reward utility occupy distinct roles: a direction that reliably \\emph{detects} a behavior may fail to \\emph{correct} it when the optimizer exploits the geometric shortcut that makes detection easy.\n91\tInference-time reranking~\\citep{papadatos2024probepenalties} and per-step process rewards~\\citep{beigi2025smart} sidestep this by avoiding optimization-loop inclusion entirely.\n92\t\\enlargethispage{2\\baselineskip}\n93\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"978d5c6d-01eb-430b-a005-ba8925173f6b","uuid":"bcd02462-8b74-4437-b60d-2bd208984e82","timestamp":"2026-05-25T17:26:31.648Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-be-idea-gen-0515-3/projects/contrastive_entrain_calib/docs/paper/sections/discussion.tex","content":"\\section{When Does Discriminability Fail as Reward Utility?}\\label{sec:discussion}\n\n\\paragraph{Root cause of the probe reward trap.}\nThe probe reward trap (\\S\\ref{sec:probe_trap}) and the cosine failures (\\S\\ref{sec:cosine_failure}) share a common geometric root.\n$\\dsyc$ encodes the \\emph{direction} of belief change but not its \\emph{evidential warrant}: valid revision and sycophantic capitulation both shift activations toward the user's position along the same direction.\nThe two reward families expose complementary faces of this blindness.\nCosine $\\rone$ penalizes all belief change indiscriminately (mode collapse, F1c--F1d); the binary probe $\\rone$ rewards all resistance regardless of input validity (stubbornness trap, $\\tof{=}0$ by step 500)---dual consequences of a direction that conflates resisting invalid challenges with refusing valid corrections.\nAlthough $\\dsyc$ separability correlates with evidence strength (\\S\\ref{sec:direction_quality}), it encodes \\emph{how much} belief changed, not whether the change was appropriate (\\S\\ref{sec:probe_trap}).\nCross-model evidence (Llama-3-8B AUROC $0.779$) confirms the limitation generalizes.\nThis contrasts with safety directions~\\citep{zhang2026latentgrpo}, where the target behavior is geometrically distinct; concept directions succeed when shortcuts are separable~\\citep{wu2026rewardhacking}.\nIndependent work corroborates: persona vectors are independent of $\\dsyc$ \\citep{kelkar2026persona}, and sycophancy sub-behaviors \\citep{vennemeyer2025sycophancy} collapse onto $\\dsyc$'s single axis.\n\n\\paragraph{GRPO results under our configuration.}\n\n\\begin{table}[t]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Sycophancy calibration methods on Qwen3-8B. Higher $\\sycon$ (harmonic mean of $\\tof$ and $\\nof$) indicates better calibration.}\n\\label{tab:main_comparison}\n\\resizebox{\\columnwidth}{!}{%\n\\begin{tabular}{@{}llcccc@{}}\n\\toprule\nMethod & Type & $\\sycon$ $\\uparrow$ & $\\tof$ $\\uparrow$ & $\\nof$ $\\uparrow$ & Step \\\\\n\\midrule\nVanilla & -- & 0.134 & 0.072 & 0.945 & -- \\\\\n\\midrule\n\\multicolumn{6}{l}{\\textit{GRPO with $\\dsyc$}} \\\\\nCosine $\\rone$ (F1a--F1d)$^a$ & RL & 0.000 & 0.000 & 1.000 & 500 \\\\\nBinary Probe $\\rone$ (F2) & RL & 0.000 & 0.000 & 0.995 & 500 \\\\\nContinuous Probe $\\rone$ (F3) & RL & 0.124 & 0.066 & 0.934 & 500 \\\\\n\\midrule\n\\multicolumn{6}{l}{\\textit{GRPO without $\\dsyc$}} \\\\\n$\\rthree$-only GRPO$^b$ & RL & 0.153 & 0.083 & 0.983 & 6500 \\\\\n\\midrule\n\\multicolumn{6}{l}{\\textit{SFT with $\\dsyc$ probe penalty}} \\\\\nSFT probe (seed 2)$^c$ & SFT & 0.393 & 0.276 & 0.680 & 500 \\\\\nSFT probe (seed 3)$^c$ & SFT & 0.407 & 0.287 & 0.696 & 1000 \\\\\n\\midrule\n\\multicolumn{6}{l}{\\textit{Reference methods}$^d$} \\\\\nActAdd ($\\alpha{=}5$) & Inference & 0.054 & 0.028 & 0.961 & -- \\\\\n\\textbf{ACT} (seed 1) & SFT & \\textbf{0.301} & \\textbf{0.182} & 0.867 & 8000 \\\\\nACT (seed 2)$^e$ & SFT & 0.286 & 0.171 & 0.862 & 7000 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\multicolumn{6}{l}{\\footnotesize $^a$All collapsed from step 1 ($\\tof{=}0$); F1d diverged at step 2160.} \\\\\n\\multicolumn{6}{l}{\\footnotesize $^b$Best of 28 checkpoints (2 seeds); only 4/28 exceed vanilla.} \\\\\n\\multicolumn{6}{l}{\\footnotesize $^c$Peak ckpt (train/eval overlap); 2/3 seeds collapse by step 2000 (mean $0.171 \\pm 0.122$).} \\\\\n\\multicolumn{6}{l}{\\footnotesize $^d$Not directly comparable: differ from GRPO along 5+ dimensions (\\S\\ref{sec:discussion}).} \\\\\n\\multicolumn{6}{l}{\\footnotesize $^e$15 ckpts, all ${>}$ vanilla. Best $\\sycon{=}0.286$ (step 7000).} \\\\\n\\end{tabular}}\n\\end{table}\n\nIf $\\dsyc$ alone caused the cosine and probe failures (\\S\\ref{sec:cosine_failure}--\\S\\ref{sec:probe_trap}), removing it should recover calibration.\n$\\rthree$-only GRPO tests this: only a minority of checkpoints across two seeds exceed vanilla, with both seeds oscillating before diverging (Table~\\ref{tab:main_comparison}; Figure~\\ref{fig:trajectory}).\n$\\dsyc$ AUROC and $\\rthree$ both remain nearly constant across checkpoints, yet $\\sycon$ fluctuates substantially.\n$\\rthree$ mirrors $\\dsyc$'s limitation: it identifies valid corrections at a negligible rate, comparable to the vanilla baseline, confirming that the asymmetry reflects the NLI hypothesis design, not behavioral collapse.\nBoth signals encode \\emph{whether} belief changed, not \\emph{whether it should have}.\n\n\\paragraph{Competing hypotheses and ablation.}\nThree explanations are consistent with these failures: (a)~$\\dsyc$ is fundamentally unsuitable as a sycophancy reward; (b)~group size$=$2 provides insufficient ranking diversity; (c)~sycophancy calibration resists scalar per-completion RL.\nTwo ablations discriminate among them (Table~\\ref{tab:ablation}).\nGRPO fails at both group sizes tested (gs$=$8: all below vanilla, terminated early) and at doubled sequence length (512 tokens, reward flat), ruling out~(b) and truncation (Table~\\ref{tab:ablation}).\nReducing ACT to GRPO's LoRA configuration still yields consistently higher $\\sycon$, with every checkpoint exceeding vanilla; under matched adapters, per-token SFT achieves $1.7{\\times}$ higher $\\sycon$ than per-completion GRPO, identifying supervision granularity as one plausible explanation~\\citep{beigi2025smart}; confounds are discussed in Limitations.\nThe probe reward trap independently supports~(a): the trap arises despite stopped gradients.\n\n\\begin{table}[t]\n\\centering\n\\small\n\\caption{Ablation: isolating supervision paradigm from LoRA configuration. All methods use Qwen3-8B with $\\rthree$ (behavioral reward). Vanilla $\\sycon{=}0.134$. $^\\dagger$Terminated early after three checkpoints showed declining trajectory. $^\\ddagger$Peak at step 7000; final checkpoint (step 8000) $\\sycon{=}0.267$.}\n\\label{tab:ablation}\n\\resizebox{\\columnwidth}{!}{%\n\\begin{tabular}{@{}llcc@{}}\n\\toprule\nMethod & LoRA config & Best $\\sycon$ & ${>}$Van. \\\\\n\\midrule\nGRPO gs$=$2 (2 seeds) & r64, $\\alpha$64, 4m & 0.153 & 4/28 \\\\\nGRPO gs$=$8$^\\dagger$ & r64, $\\alpha$64, 4m & 0.085 & 0/3 \\\\\n\\midrule\nACT reduced-LoRA$^\\ddagger$ & r64, $\\alpha$64, 4m & 0.326 & 16/16 \\\\\nACT full s1 & r64, $\\alpha$128, 7m & 0.301 & 16/16 \\\\\nACT full s2 & r64, $\\alpha$128, 7m & 0.286 & 15/15 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}}\n\\end{table}\n\n\\paragraph{ACT vs.\\ probe-based methods.}\nACT's advantage over GRPO is categorical: even ACT's worst checkpoint outperforms GRPO's best, with held-out $\\sycon$ of $0.284$ confirming generalization beyond training data (Limitations).\nSFT with a differentiable probe penalty achieves higher peak $\\sycon$ on the training set (Table~\\ref{tab:main_comparison}), but these scores reflect full train/eval overlap and the advantage is transient: probe gaming (\\S\\ref{sec:probe_trap}) eliminates the regularization signal, and the model overfits to below vanilla by step 2000 in two of three seeds (mean $\\sycon{=}0.171 \\pm 0.122$).\nThree temporal patterns emerge: GRPO probe rewards cause immediate behavioral death ($\\tof{=}0$); SFT probe penalties yield initially high but unsustainable calibration; ACT sacrifices peak for stability by eliminating probe dependence (31/31 ${>}$ vanilla, with held-out generalization confirmed).\n\n\\paragraph{Inference-time probes and future directions.}\nDiscriminability and reward utility occupy distinct roles: a direction that reliably \\emph{detects} a behavior may fail to \\emph{correct} it when the optimizer exploits the geometric shortcut that makes detection easy.\nInference-time reranking~\\citep{papadatos2024probepenalties} and per-step process rewards~\\citep{beigi2025smart} sidestep this by avoiding optimization-loop inclusion entirely.\n\\enlargethispage{2\\baselineskip}\n","numLines":93,"startLine":1,"totalLines":93}}}
